title: Lt. Gen. Spellmon’s message to Maui on first anniversary of wildfires
description: Lt. Gen. Scott A. Spellmon, 55th Chief of Engineers and Commanding General of the United States Army Corps of Engineers, speaks directly to the community of Maui about USACE’s ongoing commitment to recovery, the progress that’s been made over the past year, and the future that is being built together for the first anniversary of the devastating wildfires that swept through Lahaina and Kula on August 8, 2023.
keywords: FEMA, Pacific Ocean Division, Lahaina, HawaiiWildfires23, County of Maui, USACE Headquarters
unit_name: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Honolulu District

transcript.text: To all our friends and partners in Maui .
Aloha . I'm Lieutenant General Scott
Spellman , chief of engineers and
commanding general of the US Army Corps
of Engineers as we approach the one
year mark since the devastating
wildfires that swept through your
island . I want to take a moment to
speak directly to you about our ongoing
commitment to your recovery and the
future . We are building together .
Over the past year , we have worked
alongside our partners at Fema state
and county agencies and our dedicated
contractors , many of whom call Maui
home . Our mission has been clear to
provide immediate relief and to lay the
foundation for a resilient and brighter
future . One of our major ongoing
projects is the development of the
Kilohana temporary housing site . This
site will provide much needed longer
term housing for wildfire survivors
offering a safe haven close to their
original homes . This allows families
to remain in their community while they
begin the process of rebuilding their
lives . The Kla Hana project is a
monumental effort from transforming
former agricultural fields into a
community of 169 housing units to
ensuring these homes are equipped with
the essential utilities , our teams are
working around the clock despite the
challenges , we are on track to
complete the site . By the end of this
year . A testament to the dedication
and hard work of everyone involved . In
addition to Klo Hana , we have made
significant strides in debris removal .
Since beginning this mission in
November of 2023 we have cleared over
97% of the affected residential
properties and nearly 50% of the
affected commercial properties . This
progress is a collaborative achievement
with many of our contractors being
local residents who share a deep
commitment to restoring Lahaina .
Looking ahead , we remain focused on
long term recovery efforts . We are
actively engaged in multiple projects
aimed at restoring infrastructure ,
protecting cultural heritage and
enhancing the resilience of your
communities against future disasters .
Commitment to Maui is unwavering the US
Army Corps of Engineers in partnership
with FEMA and local agencies will stand
by you every step of the way we know
the road to recovery is long , but
together we're going to rebuild , heal
and emerge stronger . The spirit of
Aloha that defines Maui and the
Hawaiian Islands has shown brightly
through these challenging times to
those families who lost loved ones .
During this terrible tragedy . We
continue to mourn with you to all
island residents , your resilience and
unity , inspire us all . We're not just
rebuilding structures . We are also
fostering hope and strength within this
incredible community to the people of
Maui . Mahalo . For your unwavering
spirit and trust .
